name: Dumbbell Thruster
summary: A full-body movement that links a front squat with an overhead press in one smooth motion. It builds leg and shoulder strength and raises the heart rate fast.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing each other, elbows slightly in front of the body.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Brace your trunk and keep your chest up.
execution: Sit into a squat, pushing your knees out over your toes, until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Keep the dumbbells at your shoulders and your torso tall.
Drive up through your whole foot and use that momentum to press the dumbbells overhead.
Finish with arms straight over your shoulders and legs extended, then lower the weights back to shoulder height and go into the next squat.
cues: Use the legs to start the press
Weights stay close to the shoulders
mistakes: Pressing before the legs finish: let the legs extend and then send the weights up.
Leaning forward in the squat: keep the chest up and elbows forward.
Lower back arching at lockout: squeeze the glutes and brace the abs.
Going too heavy: pick a weight you can control for all reps, since fatigue builds quickly.
